question: Pearl — DEF, 11-9, a 5v5 has just traded down to 3v3, you are holding A (near A Ramps / A Main) after your team picked two attackers. No push is confirmed yet. How do you play the hold?

options.label: Hold your angle and gather info before committing — let the minimap and sound tell you where the 3 attackers actually go
options.explication_courte: In an even 3v3 mid-round, information is the highest-value resource: don't over-rotate or over-peek on a guess. Holding a safe angle and reading the minimap/sound lets you commit only when you KNOW the attack's direction, keeping every duel on your terms.

sources_option.citation: Defenders extract decisions from the minimap and sound; commit rotations only on confirmed info, not on a guess

options.label: Push out into A Main aggressively to hunt a third pick and take control before they group
options.explication_courte: Pushing out in a 3v3 gambles the numbers you just earned — if you die into their space, your two teammates are now defending short-handed. Aggression here trades a solid even hold for a coinflip you didn't need.

sources_option.citation: Pushing into unknown space when even on numbers risks giving back the advantage; hold and let them come to you

options.label: Rotate early toward the other site to reinforce, assuming the attack goes elsewhere
options.explication_courte: Reinforcing can be right if you have a read, but rotating on assumption abandons your area for free and can be faked. Without confirmed info, leaving A early risks handing the attackers exactly the site you just vacated.

sources_option.citation: Rotate on confirmed information; rotating early on an unconfirmed read can be baited by a fake and opens your vacated site

options.label: Dump your ultimate and util into A now to zone the choke pre-emptively
options.explication_courte: Spending your ult and util on empty space before any push is confirmed wastes them — if the attackers hit the other site or wait you out, you've burned resources you needed for the actual fight or retake.

sources_option.citation: Deploying util into empty space on a guess wastes non-regenerable resources needed for the confirmed engagement

explication_longue: This is an information-discipline decision, the defensive twin of duel selection. On Pearl at 11-9, your team has just traded a 5v5 down to an even 3v3, and you are holding A near the Ramps/Main with no push yet confirmed. The highest-EV move is the patient one: hold a safe angle and let the minimap and sound tell you where the three attackers are actually going before you do anything. Information is the resource that decides even mid-rounds — over-rotating or over-peeking on a guess is how defenders throw away numbers they just earned. Pushing out into A Main to hunt a third pick is the costly error: in a 3v3 you gamble the advantage, and dying into their space leaves your two teammates short-handed. Rotating early to reinforce the other site is genuinely acceptable if you have a read, but on an unconfirmed assumption it abandons your area for free and is exactly what a fake exploits — leave A too early and the attackers take the site you just vacated. Dumping your ult and util into an empty A pre-emptively is the faute: spent on a guess, those resources are gone when the real fight or retake arrives. Hold, read, and commit only when the info is real.

sources.citation: Defensive decisions run on confirmed information from minimap and sound; hold and commit only when the attack's direction is known
